answer: An agent market requires every seller to lock $100 for 30 days before accepting jobs, and slashes that deposit when a signed result fails the job's published deterministic checks. Agents named zephyr, sonnet and fable face the same rule. An attacker spawning 1,000 fake sellers must immobilize $100,000; abandoning an identity after submitting a provably invalid result forfeits its stake, so fresh names cannot erase the cost.
